visibility: A state is visible when an ordinary open, catalog scan, or served subject can observe the entry or result it describes.

primitive.basis: BSD flock on a lock file opened O_CLOEXEC: an exclusive holder blocked a second exclusive request, two shared holders coexisted and blocked an exclusive request, and the lock was released 2.8 ms after its holder was SIGKILLed (results/platform.json). POSIX record locks (lockf/fcntl) are rejected: the lock silently vanished when the same process closed an unrelated descriptor for the file.
primitive.unmeasured: Only macOS APFS was measured, and CI runs only ubuntu-latest. Network filesystems can emulate flock with POSIX record locks, which behave like the rejected lockf. The format foundation therefore probes the application home at setup instead of trusting the platform: cross-process exclusion, survival of the lock when an unrelated descriptor for the lock file closes, and no-replace publication; a home that fails any probe is refused as unverifiable.

hierarchy.name: home
hierarchy.protects: layout migration, brief global enumeration for catalog scans and sweeps, and moving quarantined entries to trash

hierarchy.name: source_alias
hierarchy.protects: slug claim, alias creation, and compare-and-swap repointing; several aliases lock in ascending slug order

hierarchy.name: repository_store
hierarchy.protects: store directory publication and removal, store records, and ref compare-and-swap; several stores lock in ascending key order. It is held only for those short steps, never across network work or a long-running Git process such as fetch, gc, or repack

hierarchy.name: provider_resource
hierarchy.path: owned by the provider storage plan
hierarchy.protects: binding, snapshot publication, pointer movement, and provider reclamation

side_locks.name: staging_entry
side_locks.acquisition: taken before cache/staging/<entry>/ is created and held by its one owner for the entry's whole life, including network work; every other process only tries it without blocking
side_locks.why_outside_the_hierarchy: It is a liveness marker nobody waits on, so holding it across network work cannot block another operation.

side_locks.name: trash_entry
side_locks.acquisition: taken before an entry is renamed into trash and held until deletion finishes; others try without blocking

side_locks.name: job_entry
side_locks.acquisition: held by the process running a fetch job for the job's whole life; reclamation tries it without blocking before deleting that job's private refs

side_locks.name: maintenance_shared
side_locks.acquisition: the store lease: held by a live subject, by an acquisition from before store publication until its alias is published, and by a fetch job from before its network work until publication. It may block only while its holder holds no hierarchy lock
side_locks.why_outside_the_hierarchy: Nobody blocks on it while holding a hierarchy lock, and its exclusive form never blocks, so it cannot close a wait cycle.

side_locks.name: maintenance_exclusive
side_locks.acquisition: never blocks; taken while holding no hierarchy lock by gc and repack, which run under it alone, and by reclamation, purge, and quarantine before their hierarchy locks. Failure defers maintenance or refuses the operation
side_locks.why_outside_the_hierarchy: Because it never waits, a long-lived lease cannot turn it into a deadlock.

rules: No network work, provider process, or long-running Git process runs while a hierarchy lock is held; gc and repack run under maintenance_exclusive alone.
Hierarchy locks are acquired in ascending rank, and within one rank in ascending key order; a lock is never re-acquired while held.
The home lock is never acquired while any narrower hierarchy lock is held.
Blocking on a side lock is allowed only while holding no hierarchy lock, and maintenance_exclusive never blocks.

Every object enters a store under the store lease, and every alias that names a store is written under that store's lease, so an exclusive maintenance holder sees a stable set of objects and referring aliases.
Lock files live under cache/locks/ and are never inside a directory that publication, purge, quarantine, or reclamation renames.

After acquiring any lock, the holder compares the locked descriptor's fstat with the path's lstat (device and inode) and releases and retries on a mismatch, because a sweep may have removed and recreated the lock file.
Liveness is decided by trying the entry's lock, not by age: a crashed holder releases within milliseconds, while no age can distinguish a slow clone from a dead one.

publication.rule: The owning hierarchy lock is held, the target path is verified absent with lstat, and the staged directory or record is renamed into place; that check under the lock is the guarantee, because every Metabrowser writer of the path takes the same lock.
publication.defense_in_depth: Where the platform offers an atomic no-replace rename it is used for the same rename: renameat2 with RENAME_NOREPLACE on Linux and renamex_np with RENAME_EXCL on macOS, called through ctypes with no new dependency. It turns a violated lock discipline into an error instead of a silent replacement.
publication.basis: On APFS os.rename replaced an existing empty directory, os.rename onto a non-empty directory failed with ENOTEMPTY, and renamex_np with RENAME_EXCL refused an existing empty directory with EEXIST (results/platform.json). renameat2 was not measured.

nothing_to_recover.action: No durable state changed before the crash.

staging_swept.action: The startup sweep finds the staging entry's lock free and deletes the entry. A SIGKILLed clone leaves its destination and a temporary pack behind (results/concurrency.json), so staging is never inside a published path.

unreferenced_store_reclaimable.action: The operating system released the crashed acquisition's lease. A published store that no alias, durable provider ref, or lease reaches is not visible; reclamation moves it to trash under the exclusive maintenance lock and the store lock, or quarantines it when its records do not validate.

trash_swept.action: The startup sweep deletes a trash entry whose lock is free.

job_refs_reclaimable.action: The job's private refs under refs/metabrowser/jobs/<job-id>/ remain until reclamation finds the job lock free and deletes them under the store lock; their objects then become unreachable and maintenance compacts or prunes them. Public refs never changed.

shared_lock_released_by_os.action: The process is gone, so its subject is gone; the operating system released the lease. Durable private refs keep promised objects reachable.

sweep_restarts.action: The sweep is idempotent and runs again at the next startup.

maintenance_rerun.action: Git writes new packs before removing old ones; the next maintenance run removes temporary files. Crash during gc was not measured.

quarantine_retained.action: Quarantine is never reclaimed automatically; inspect and purge report the retained path.

alias_cas_atomic.action: The alias record is replaced by one atomic rename after its generation check, so it names either the old or the new store.

interleaving.purpose: Exhaustively explore every interleaving of the listed processes over one source alias S and one store K. Each step is atomic: its acquisitions, the first branch whose conditions hold, the branch's effects, and its releases. A step whose blocking acquisition is unavailable is not enabled; a step whose non-blocking acquisition fails takes its busy branch.
invariants: An alias never names a store that is absent from repository-stores (trashed, reclaimed, or never published).
Hierarchy locks are acquired in ascending rank and key order, blocking side-lock acquisitions happen with no hierarchy lock held, and the exclusive maintenance lock never blocks.
Some process can always move until every process has ended, and every lock is released at the end.
Every executed event is a transition from the process's current machine state whose contended locks equal the locks held during the step.

acquisition_without_lease.note: The design this check replaced: no store lease, and the alias commit does not re-verify the store under the store lock.
